item.title: KAIST Engineers Build Light-Activated Buttons From Laser-Programmed Shape Memory Alloy
item.summary: KAIST researchers developed flat nickel–titanium alloy sheets that pop into 3D button shapes when hit with near-infrared light, using a single UV laser step that both cuts kirigami patterns and creates a photothermal absorption layer — a wirelessly actuated, motor-free interface with direct implications for agent-controlled robotics and wearables.
